lines.text: Which is a feature of the action of insulin?
The answer is: it promotes protein synthesis.
Insulin is the builder, stacking bricks of protein, one on top of the other.
That is protein synthesis, and insulin promotes it.
(laugh) Look at the potassium ions running through the door. Insulin drives potassium into cells.
That is why insulin is used to treat hyperkalaemia.
Calcium and phosphate metabolism belongs to parathyroid hormone and activated vitamin D, not insulin.
Remember: insulin promotes protein synthesis.
Which change is caused by prolonged vomiting due to pyloric stenosis?
The answer is a rise in arterial pCO2.
This baby has prolonged vomiting, and the acid keeps pouring into the basin.
Losing the stomach acid causes a hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis, with a rise in pH and raised bicarbonate.
Gastric juice is rich in potassium, so hypokalaemia follows, with a hypovolaemic state and raised urea.
(sigh) To compensate, the tired lungs breathe slowly. This is hypoventilation.
And slow breathing lets the carbon dioxide build up, so arterial pCO2 rises.
Remember: prolonged vomiting gives alkalosis, and a rise in arterial pCO2.

A patient on the surgical ward has chronic renal impairment. The plasma creatinine is two hundred and twenty-five, and the glomerular filtration rate is twenty-five millilitres per minute. Which statement is correct regarding the patient's renal function?
The answer: inulin clearance can be used to estimate GFR.
The kidney filter is struggling. The GFR is only twenty-five.
And the creatinine flag is raised, two hundred and twenty-five.
A normal adult GFR averages one hundred and twenty-five millilitres a minute, or 180 litres a day.
Inulin is filtered freely, so inulin clearance can be used to estimate GFR.
The entire plasma volume, about 3 litres, is filtered about 60 times each day.
But the rate of urine production is dominated by tubular function, not by GFR.
Remember: inulin clearance estimates the GFR.
